My mother passed away  at home earlier this month, and I was told the procedure in obtaining a death certificate by the attending paramedics and police.
What seemed to be a straightforward line of contact turned into a complete farce,in what was and is a very stressful and upsetting time.After receiving a call from the coroners office a pretty simple and sympathetic Q&A conversation took place.It was then explained that the next step was that  a report from the coroner would be sent to her Doctors surgery for a signature to agree with the coroners findings. Then from there to the medical examiners office for confirmation and finally onto the Registry office.
The coroners report was sent off on the same day that I had spoken to them,and that l would be contacted within a couple of days by the ME.A week went by and I had not received any calls. I then got in touch with the ME only to be informed that they had not received any notification from Brinsworth surgery.
After several phone calls to all involved, it turned out that the surgery had sent the report back to the coroners office instead of the medical examiners office,and they had sent it back on the same day as they had received it.
The matter was finally resolved with help from the medical examiners office, and I was then able to get an appointment with the registrar.
During one of many conversations with the surgery, out of curiosity I asked if they had the phone number for the medical examiners office, they told me the number that they had,to which I pointed out, was the wrong number, and I then gave them the correct one!!!
This is not the first time that I have issues with this surgery,and after having treatment in the Rotherham hospital last year, my mother was discharged and given slight changes in her prescription. The changes being quantity wise.After several days of no medication being provided, the local pharmacy said that they had still not received any communication from Brinsworth surgery. After  calls to the doctors I was told that they had received the drug prescribed from the hospital but not the dosage required. I asked the doctor if they had spoken to the hospital,as my mother had now taken no medication for a few days, the doctors response was that it's not our responsibility to keep asking and they had called twice in the last few days,but had not got a reply. I made ONE phone call to the hospital, explaining the situation, they apologised and a replacement prescription with the dosage was sent the same day to Brinwsorth.
